source_used: Claims Journal carrying Bloomberg (two articles, 14 and 15 Oct); Bloomberg blocked
key_facts: Hearing on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 before US District Judge Edward Davila in San Jose on Apple's trade secret suit against OpenAI
Apple sued in July alleging OpenAI conspired to extract confidential information from former Apple employees; OpenAI denies it
Apple asks for a preliminary injunction; OpenAI separately asks to dismiss the suit
The judge said he is "highly likely" to grant the injunction but called a proposed forensic inspection of devices a "huge ask"
Just before the hearing OpenAI said a former employee who returned to Apple sent over a hundred confidential OpenAI files to personal accounts
The day before, the judge ordered OpenAI to speed up handing over documents
quote_evidence: The judge in Apple Inc.’s high-stakes trade-secret theft case against OpenAI said he’s “highly likely” to grant the iPhone maker an injunction barring use of its proprietary information by former employees now at the artificial intelligence startup.
“OpenAI is developing a new family of devices designed for the AI era,” the company said in an October court filing. “OpenAI has no need or desire for Apple’s trade secrets.”
why_it_matters_hint: A ruling for Apple could slow OpenAI's hardware plans.
notes: Bloomberg blocked; read Bloomberg text on Claims Journal. The judge has not yet ruled. Pool follow_up_of field showed an odd id; matched to our 14 Oct item on the judge ordering OpenAI to hand over hiring records.
title: Apple, OpenAI Head to Court in High-Stakes AI Trade Secret Fight
